stem: The force acting perpendicularly on a unit area of a surface is called __________.
solution: Pressure is the force acting per unit area on a surface.

stem: For the same force, pressure is greater when the area of contact is __________.
solution: Pressure is inversely related to area; a smaller area gives greater pressure for the same force.

stem: A sharp knife cuts better than a blunt one because its thin edge exerts __________.
options: greater pressure due to a smaller area
solution: The small edge area concentrates the force into a high pressure, cutting easily.

stem: The broad, flat foundation of a building is made wide to __________.
solution: A larger area reduces the pressure on the soil, giving stability.

stem: Liquids exert pressure on the __________ of their container.
solution: A liquid exerts pressure on the bottom and on the walls of its container.

stem: Pressure exerted by a liquid __________ with depth.
solution: Liquid pressure increases with depth because of the weight of the liquid above.

stem: Dam walls are built thicker at the bottom because water pressure __________ there.
solution: Water pressure is highest at the bottom, so dams are made thicker there to withstand it.

stem: The layer of air surrounding the Earth is called the __________.
solution: The atmosphere is the blanket of air surrounding the Earth.

stem: The pressure exerted by the weight of air on the Earth's surface is called __________ pressure.
solution: Atmospheric pressure is due to the weight of the column of air above a surface.

stem: Atmospheric pressure __________ as we go higher up in the atmosphere.
solution: Air is thinner at higher altitudes, so atmospheric pressure decreases with height.

stem: A rubber sucker sticks to a smooth surface because of __________.
solution: Pressing out the air leaves lower pressure inside, so atmospheric pressure holds the sucker in place.

stem: We do not feel crushed by atmospheric pressure because __________.
options: the pressure inside our body balances it
solution: The pressure inside our body equals the outside atmospheric pressure, so they balance.

stem: Moving air is called __________.
solution: Wind is air in motion, caused by differences in air pressure.

stem: Air moves from a region of __________ pressure to a region of __________ pressure.
solution: Winds blow from high-pressure regions to low-pressure regions.

stem: When air is heated, it __________.
solution: Heated air expands, becomes lighter and rises, creating a low-pressure region below.

stem: The uneven heating of land and water causes __________ in coastal areas.
solution: Differences in heating of land and sea create sea breezes by day and land breezes by night.

stem: During the day, a cool breeze blows from the sea towards the land; this is the __________ breeze.
solution: By day the land heats faster, air rises over it, and cool air blows in from the sea — the sea breeze.

stem: The uneven heating of the Earth between the equator and the poles causes __________.
solution: Uneven heating of the Earth drives large winds and the seasonal monsoon.

stem: The seasonal winds that bring heavy rain to India in summer are the __________.
solution: The monsoon winds carry moisture from the sea and bring rain to India.

stem: A violent storm with very strong swirling winds and low pressure at the centre is called a __________.
solution: A cyclone is a large, violent storm with strong rotating winds around a low-pressure centre.

stem: The calm central region of a cyclone is called the __________.
solution: The eye of a cyclone is its calm, low-pressure centre.

stem: Cyclones form over __________.
solution: Cyclones develop over warm ocean waters, where moist rising air feeds the storm.

stem: A thunderstorm is usually accompanied by __________.
solution: Thunderstorms bring lightning, thunder, rain and gusty winds.

stem: The safest action during a thunderstorm and lightning is to __________.
options: stay indoors and away from open fields
hold a metal umbrella in the open
solution: Staying inside and away from tall isolated objects reduces the risk of a lightning strike.

stem: Standing under a tall isolated tree during lightning is dangerous because __________.
options: lightning tends to strike tall objects
solution: Lightning often strikes the tallest object around, so a lone tall tree is dangerous.

stem: A device fitted on tall buildings to protect them from lightning is called a __________.
solution: A lightning conductor safely carries the lightning's charge to the ground.

stem: A tornado is a __________.
options: dark, funnel-shaped, rapidly rotating column of air
solution: A tornado is a violently rotating funnel of air extending from a storm cloud to the ground.

stem: The instrument used to measure atmospheric pressure is the __________.
solution: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

stem: The instrument used to measure wind speed is the __________.
solution: An anemometer measures the speed of the wind.

stem: A sudden fall in atmospheric pressure on a barometer is often a warning of an approaching __________.
solution: A sharp pressure drop often signals stormy weather is on the way.

stem: During high-speed winds over a roof, the roof may be blown off because the pressure __________ the roof is lower.
solution: Fast wind over the roof lowers the pressure above it, so higher pressure inside pushes it up and off.

stem: The faster air moves over a surface, the __________ the pressure it exerts.
solution: Increased air speed is accompanied by reduced pressure, an important principle in weather and flight.

stem: The best protection before a cyclone strikes a coastal area is to __________.
options: move to a safe shelter and follow warnings
stay in a boat at sea
solution: Heeding cyclone warnings and moving to safe shelters saves lives.

stem: The huge rise in sea level near the coast during a cyclone, which floods low areas, is called a __________.
solution: A storm surge is the abnormal rise in seawater during a cyclone, causing coastal flooding.

stem: Weather satellites help by __________.
options: tracking storms and giving early warnings
solution: Satellites monitor storms from space, enabling early warnings that save lives.

stem: When you drink through a straw, the liquid rises because you reduce the pressure inside and __________.
options: atmospheric pressure pushes the liquid up
solution: Sucking lowers the pressure in the straw, and outside atmospheric pressure forces the liquid up.

stem: A balloon bursts when it is over-inflated because the internal air pressure exceeds __________.
solution: When the inside pressure is too great for the rubber to hold, the balloon bursts.

stem: Pressure is calculated as force divided by __________.
solution: Pressure = force / area.

stem: Camels can walk on soft sand without sinking because their broad feet __________.
solution: Broad feet increase the contact area, reducing the pressure on the sand.

stem: The nib of a pen and the tip of a nail are made pointed to __________.
options: exert high pressure over a small area
solution: A small tip area gives high pressure, letting the nail pierce or the pen mark easily.

stem: Air, like liquids, exerts pressure __________.
solution: Air (a fluid) exerts pressure in all directions, just like liquids.

stem: A region of low atmospheric pressure is often associated with __________ weather.
solution: Low pressure often brings rising moist air, clouds and stormy weather.

stem: The main driving cause of all winds on the Earth is __________.
options: differences in air pressure due to uneven heating
solution: Uneven heating creates pressure differences that set air in motion as wind.

stem: Emptying and crushing a plastic bottle after sucking out air demonstrates the effect of __________.
solution: With less air inside, the greater outside atmospheric pressure crushes the bottle.

stem: A high-pressure region generally brings __________ weather.
solution: High pressure usually brings sinking air, clear skies and calm weather.

stem: Ventilators are placed near the ceiling of a room because warm air __________.
solution: Warm, used air rises and leaves through high ventilators, allowing fresh air in.

stem: The main reason mountaineers carry oxygen cylinders at great heights is that __________.
options: air pressure and oxygen are low there
it is too cold to breathe
solution: At high altitudes low air pressure means less oxygen, so climbers carry oxygen.

stem: A cyclone is given advance warning so that people can __________.
options: watch it closely on the coast
solution: Early warnings let people evacuate and prepare, reducing loss of life and property.

stem: The overall relationship shown in this chapter is that differences in __________ cause wind, storms and cyclones.
solution: Pressure and temperature differences drive winds, storms and cyclones.

stem: Which of these should NOT be done during a cyclone warning?
options: Going out to the coast to watch the sea
solution: Going out to watch the sea is dangerous; the others are sensible precautions.
